title: CTO Interview With Juan Rey, senior VP and general manager of Calibre and CTO of Siemens EDA
gist: Siemens EDA CTO and Calibre GM Juan Rey says customers face an industry-wide reinvention driven by sub-14-angstrom nodes, 2.5D/3D integration, power/sustainability pressure and complexity-versus-schedule crunch. Siemens' AI stance is explicitly conservative: ML surrogate models and multi-agent assistants for exploration and debugging, but signoff stays on deterministic Calibre engines with engineers accountable.

insights.claim: Rey says the move from 14 angstroms down to 10 and beyond, combined with the shift from 2D to 2.5D and 3D integration, is creating entirely new physical and algorithmic problems nobody had to solve a few years ago.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Rising physical-verification complexity supports demand for EDA tools such as Calibre.
insights.locator: If you look at the technical side

insights.claim: Rey says power efficiency and sustainability have shot to the top of customers' priorities, with pressure to radically cut power consumption and conserve water and energy across the full lifecycle of massive systems.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Power and water constraints are becoming design-tool requirements, not just facility issues.
insights.locator: At the same time, power efficiency

insights.claim: Near-term, Rey expects physical and manufacturing barriers to get tougher as nodes shrink toward 10 angstroms and below, especially managing thermal and mechanical interactions in multi-die 2.5D and 3D setups.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Thermal/mechanical multi-die analysis is a growth area for verification vendors.
insights.locator: Near-term, the physical and manufacturing barriers

themes.theme: AI as exploration aid, not signoff replacement

insights.claim: Siemens EDA does not use AI to replace heavy-duty signoff engines; it uses machine learning to build fast surrogate models that let engineers explore large design spaces earlier, before final signoff.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Positions incumbent signoff engines as defensible against AI-native disruption.
insights.quote: we don’t use it to blindly replace heavy-duty sign-off engines
insights.locator: And when it comes to AI

insights.claim: Rey argues deterministic, physics-grounded verification still matters because exploring a promising option is not the same as proving a design is ready for signoff or manufacturing, and AI should not blur the line between a recommendation and a verified result.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Signoff trust is the moat for Calibre; AI agents are layered on top rather than substituting.
insights.quote: AI can help engineers work through more possibilities, but it shouldn’t blur the line between a recommendation and a verified result.

insights.claim: Calibre has used AI internally for years to accelerate development and improve core algorithms, and Rey expects the biggest changes to come from agentic AI aimed at improving customer productivity.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Agentic workflow features are the next monetization lever for EDA vendors.
insights.locator: we have been using AI to accelerate development

insights.claim: Siemens is exploring multi-agent approaches that help engineers investigate physical-verification issues, gather context and surface next steps, with engineers remaining responsible for decisions and final verification relying on qualified deterministic Calibre flows.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: AI features aim to cut routine debug effort, potentially increasing tool stickiness.
insights.locator: LLMs and AI are enabling us

themes.theme: Human costs and business-model risks of AI

insights.claim: Rey warns that AI lets engineers do more in the same time but teams face mounting cognitive load and mental fatigue, and there is a real risk of eroding junior engineering expertise if people lean entirely on automation.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Productivity gains from AI may be offset by talent-pipeline erosion, a long-term industry risk.
insights.quote: There’s also a real risk of eroding foundational junior engineering expertise
insights.locator: Another big one that people don’t talk about

insights.claim: Rey cites rapidly shifting AI business models, heavy infrastructure costs, and constant re-evaluation of software ROI and licensing as customer business challenges, and says Siemens expects every internal AI investment to demonstrate measurable value.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: EDA licensing models may shift as AI changes usage patterns and customers scrutinize ROI.
insights.locator: And then there’s the business side
